factProposals.value: Idempotency is enforced by an in-memory claim-based store; no external queue (Redis Streams or SQS) is connected yet.
Structured logs are written as single-line JSON to stdout/stderr; nothing ships them to a log aggregator yet.

decisions.statement: Idempotency uses one atomic claim() call rather than a separate has()-then-set() pair.
decisions.rationale: a check-then-set pair would race under concurrent re-delivery of the same job; a single atomic operation cannot.

decisions.statement: A logging failure (e.g. a circular payload passed as context) is caught and replaced with a fallback log line instead of being allowed to throw.
decisions.rationale: logging must never be the reason a job fails to process — that's one of this story's own named failure paths.

limitations.statement: The idempotency store is in-memory only: a process restart loses every claimed key, and it is not shared across multiple worker processes.
No real job queue or external API call exists yet — 'processing' in this story is the idempotency check and its log trail, not real work.
